whatItIs.text: An underground stem tuber from the nightshade family, and one of the world's staple crops; waxy types hold for salads, floury ones fluff for mash and roasties.

historyNote.text: The potato was domesticated in the Andes around present-day southern Peru and northwestern Bolivia some 7,000-10,000 years ago, and crossed to Europe with the Spanish in the second half of the 16th century; over 5,000 varieties are grown today.

howToChoose.text: Choose firm, heavy potatoes without sprouts, cuts, or green patches — greening means solanine, which should be cut away generously or the potato skipped.

storage.text: Keep in a cool, dark, well-ventilated paper sack or basket — never the fridge, and away from onions.

useItUp.text: Sprouting potatoes still cook: rub off the sprouts, peel, and boil, roast, or mash — just skip anything green; tired ones shine as gnocchi or soup thickener.

substitutions.note: sweeter, softer, faster to cook; different starch behaviour
for lighter mash; add butter or cream for body
